cjk_cell_fix.rule: a wide glyph OWNS the cells it covers: `cellWidth` (never a character count) says how many, the covered cells render as NOTHING, and link()/label() refuse to write into them.
cjk_cell_fix.mechanism_measured: the removed loop wrote ONE array slot per character while advancing cellWidth(char) per iteration, so the cell a wide glyph covers kept rendering a background space: the row came out 6 cells wider than its 34-cell grid, and the layout's own clamp then cut the box's closing border. The clamp is where the border is lost, which is why the defect reproduced at every width and with a single wide glyph.
arms: every line's cellWidth <= cols at 120/80/48/34, and a boxed body row ENDS ON ITS BORDER COLUMN (cellWidth == colEnd + 1)
the ASCII control keeps the identical geometry, so the fix is not a special case
